standard_prerequisites.name: The dualizing complex and module of a curve
standard_prerequisites.use: Statement lines 1176-1178: omega_X^bullet and omega_X are as in this lemma; the right hand side chi(X, omega_X^bullet) is defined via them.

standard_prerequisites.name: The dualizing complex in the Cohen-Macaulay case
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1200-1203: in the CM equidimensional case omega_X^bullet = omega_X[1], which yields the second formula from the first.

core_obligations: Definition and well-definedness (proof lines 1185-1197): chi(X, omega_X^bullet) is defined as the alternating sum of dim_k H^i(X, omega_X^bullet); it is well defined because omega_X^bullet lies in D^b_Coh(O_X) and, more concretely, because H^i(X, omega_X^bullet) = Ext^i(O_X, omega_X^bullet) = H^{-i}(X, O_X) by duality, which is finite dimensional and nonzero only for i = 0, -1.
The first formula (lines 1194-1196): the same computation H^i(X, omega_X^bullet) = H^{-i}(X, O_X) proves chi(X, O_X) = chi(X, omega_X^bullet).

The Cohen-Macaulay formula (lines 1200-1203): if X is Cohen-Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension 1, then omega_X^bullet = omega_X[1], so the cohomological shifts move the dimensions by one sign and chi(X, O_X) = -chi(X, omega_X).
proof_roadmap: Define the right hand side as an alternating sum and justify finiteness through the duality isomorphism.
Read off the first formula from H^i(omega^bullet) = H^{-i}(O_X).
Specialize to the CM case using omega^bullet = omega[1].
difficulty_reason: Duality formula (statement 1173-1184, proof 1185-1203): the Euler characteristics of O_X and the dualizing complex agree, and in the Cohen-Macaulay equidimensional case chi(O_X) = -chi(omega_X) - the proof is a short complete computation through the duality isomorphism Ext^i(O_X, omega^bullet) = H^{-i}(O_X) and the CM identification omega^bullet = omega[1]; no verification is omitted. H2: duality bookkeeping.
